source_policy: Primary documentation, direct testimony and explicitly marked access-limited leads. Original authored prompts are not empirical findings.

sources.title: Toon Boom: set drawing exposure
sources.supported_scope: Drawing exposure can be set to one, two, three or a custom number of frames.
sources.limits: This is an animation-authoring control, not a video-model prompt guarantee.

sources.title: Toon Boom: drawing timing and transformation timing
sources.supported_scope: Drawing-layer and transformation-layer timing are independently controllable.
sources.limits: Tool capabilities do not prove the named generative engines implement equivalent controls.

sources.title: Adobe: principles of animation
sources.supported_scope: General principles of anticipation, staging, overlap, follow-through, exaggeration and arcs.
sources.limits: The catalog's exact combat poses, timings and risk hypotheses are original design proposals, not summaries or empirical findings from this source.

sources.title: Adobe: time effects
sources.supported_scope: Distinguishes duplicate whole frames, frame blending and pixel-motion synthesis; documents Posterize Time.
sources.limits: A post effect cannot repair an incorrect source pose or recover ungenerated action.

sources.title: Clip Studio Paint: speed and focus lines
sources.supported_scope: Directional speed lines and convergent focus lines have distinct controllable geometry.
sources.limits: Compiler restoration and actor-protection rules are authored choices.

sources.title: WildBrain artists on line boil, via Toon Boom
sources.supported_scope: Small contour variation can recreate a hand-redrawn look; line, texture and deformation boil are separable.
sources.limits: Not evidence that line boil is a universal Sushio or Imaishi characteristic.

sources.title: Adobe: cameras, lights and points of interest
sources.supported_scope: Camera position, orientation and field of view are separate properties.
sources.limits: Catalog camera staging and contact windows are original editorial prescriptions.

sources.title: Adobe: camera and light properties
sources.supported_scope: Light direction, shadow softness, intensity and distance falloff are distinct controls.
sources.limits: No numeric anime-generation lighting preset is established.

sources.title: Nikon: fisheye viewpoint examples
sources.supported_scope: Fisheye projection and viewpoint produce characteristic curved wide views.
sources.limits: No specific AI lens millimeter setting or guaranteed anatomical preservation is claimed.

sources.title: Adobe: Cartoon and stylize effects
sources.supported_scope: Edge rendering, color quantization and shading smoothness are separable image operations.
sources.limits: A cartoon filter is not a substitute for authored anime drawings; exact two-tone designs here are original recipes.

sources.title: Anime Style: Nakamura original cube-fragment illustration
sources.supported_scope: Publisher identifies cubic fragments as a motif familiar from Nakamura's work.
sources.limits: Does not establish invention or the origin of the fan nickname Yutapon cubes.

sources.title: Nakamura interview, WEB Anime Style 2003, translated 2016
sources.supported_scope: Nakamura discusses quick/slow contrasts before a sword lands and animation on ones.
sources.limits: The translation was readable; the original style.fm page could not be retrieved. No universal bounce formula is supported.

sources.title: Makiko Kanada and Masatsune Noguchi interview
sources.supported_scope: Witnesses describe scale, perspective/layout decisions and timing experiments.
sources.limits: Specific fist and pose-snapping recipes are authored interpretations; not every perspective error is intentional.

sources.title: TRIGGER interview on Promare
sources.supported_scope: Studio confirms Imaishi's Kanada influence and discusses fire dragons and hand-drawn/3DCG integration.
sources.limits: The interviewer uses Kanada dragon; the source does not define a universal geometric or line-boil preset.

sources.title: Shinya Ohira interview
sources.supported_scope: Ohira discusses vivid expression and animation-specific deformation.
sources.limits: Does not endorse accidental anatomy failures or make all his work rough ink.

sources.title: Shinji Hashimoto official Matrix interview, preserved transcript
sources.supported_scope: Hashimoto discusses atmospheric sketch-like rendering and action reference.
sources.limits: Third-party archive of a 2002 official interview; charcoal impact frames are an authored extension.

sources.title: Satoshi Nakano interview on Inu-Oh
sources.supported_scope: Nakano praises the realism and clothing movement in Matsumoto's drawings for that production.
sources.limits: Does not establish universal naturalistic physics or a prescribed punching technique.

sources.title: Ichiro Itano interview, 2014
sources.supported_scope: Itano describes near/middle/far missiles on ones/twos/threes, changing cadence with depth, camera following and spatial direction.
sources.limits: Exact trajectories in this catalog remain authored and require explicit path bindings.

sources.title: Shueisha interview with Hiroyuki Imaishi
sources.supported_scope: Imaishi distinguishes physical movement speed from speed conveyed through information density.
sources.limits: Does not supply a universal fps or motion-scale setting.

sources.title: Sushio interview on Kill la Kill
sources.supported_scope: Indexed interview passage describes a priority of understandable, enjoyable action.
sources.limits: Full page returned an access error. This is a limited-access lead, not a basis for an exact geometric signature or historical line-boil claim.

sources.title: Spencer Wan and Jerry Nguyen practitioner discussion
sources.supported_scope: Wan comments on selective shadow omission in Matsumoto's animation.
sources.limits: Aesthetic observation, not Matsumoto's own formal rule. The standardized history of kagenashi was not verified with 100% certainty.

sources.title: Benjamin Faure production interview
sources.supported_scope: Discusses purposeful impact-frame use and 3D layout preparation for 2D work.
sources.limits: No universal accent length or specific charcoal/starburst recipe is established.

sources.title: Wan2.1 original T2V implementation
sources.supported_scope: n_prompt, CFG guide_scale, scheduler shift and 4n+1 frame count.
sources.limits: Main branch observed on research date; pin a revision before implementing a production adapter.

sources.title: Wan2.1 14B Diffusers official model card
sources.supported_scope: Demonstrates negative_prompt and an 81-frame export at 15fps.
sources.limits: Example export rate is not universal native cadence. Audit stock negatives for conflicts.

sources.title: LTX-Video inference implementation
sources.supported_scope: Exposes negative_prompt, frame_rate and media conditioning arguments.
sources.limits: Actual negative effect depends on inference configuration; not an LTX-2 profile.

sources.title: LTX-Video pipeline
sources.supported_scope: Guidance scale one corresponds to no classifier-free guidance.
sources.limits: Configuration-dependent finding, not a benchmark of prompt phrases.

sources.title: LTXV 13B 0.9.8 distilled preset
sources.supported_scope: Both passes use guidance_scale one and stg_scale zero.
sources.limits: Do not change a distilled preset solely to activate negative conditioning.

sources.title: Runway Gen-3 retirement notice
sources.supported_scope: Gen-3 Alpha retired July8,2026; Turbo July30,2026.
sources.limits: The old prompting guide has been replaced; historical negative-prompt support was not reverified.

sources.title: Kling VIDEO 3.0 Omni guide
sources.supported_scope: Documents start/end frames, multiple image references, elements and shot-level instructions.
sources.limits: Vendor capability descriptions do not prove exact contact fidelity; generic Kling API negatives/fps remain unverified.

sources.title: BytePlus video-generation API
sources.supported_scope: Official entry point for checking the selected Seedance endpoint.
sources.limits: Page retrieval did not expose the complete schema; no generic negative_prompt, motion_scale or fps contract was verified.

sources.title: SQLite UPSERT
sources.supported_scope: ON CONFLICT allows targeted update on uniqueness conflict; introduced in3.24.0.
sources.limits: Does not bypass NOT NULL or CHECK failures.

sources.title: SQLite aggregate ordering
sources.supported_scope: Concatenation order is arbitrary unless explicitly controlled.
sources.limits: The supplied examples retrieve ordered rows and join in application code.

sources.title: SQLite datatype affinity
sources.supported_scope: VARCHAR length annotations are not enforced in ordinary SQLite.
sources.limits: Validation here checks lengths without changing the requested schema.
